known_differences_from_fetch_script: Server-side filter: the script sends 'OffenseYear >= 2018 AND OffenseYear <= 2024 AND UCRdesc IN (9 categories)' (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:95-100). The contract where needs {start}/{end} dates, so it filters on OffenseDate instead. OffenseDate is epoch ms in UTC and OffenseYear is the America/New_York local year: on raw_cache.parquet the local-time year of OffenseDate equals OffenseYear on 0 mismatching rows of 297,725, while the UTC year mismatches on 236 rows. The OffenseDate range is 2018-01-01T05:00Z to 2025-01-01T04:35Z. The where window therefore runs from {start} 00:00 UTC to {end} 05:00 UTC, a superset of the local-year window, and year_field=OffenseYear then applies the script's exact year filter (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:430-436). On the archived pull the result is identical. On a live pull the result is identical as long as the service stores OffenseDate in UTC with a year-end offset of at most 5 hours (EST).

StatDesc whitespace: the script strips StatDesc before lookup (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:404). The raw data has one value with a trailing space, 'Petty Theft POCKET-PICKING ' (281 rows, raw_cache_profile.json StatDesc distinct). The larceny rule lists that exact raw spelling next to the 89 offense_mapping.csv values. On raw_cache.parquet, an unstripped exact match over these 90 values keeps 173,652 rows, the same count as the script's stripped map (README.md:42). A new whitespace variant on a live pull would be kept by the script but dropped by the contract, unless the runner strips values.

Offense matching is case-sensitive (case_sensitive=true), matching the script's exact dict lookup (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:419). No two raw StatDesc values differ only by case (checked on raw_cache.parquet), so case-insensitive matching would give the same rows.

The script's completeness check reports StatDesc values that are neither mapped nor in EXCLUDED_STATDESC (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:237-321, 409-417). It is QA only. Unknown values are dropped both there and here. The contract cannot express the 76-value explicit exclusion list or the warning.

No de-duplication: the script only counts duplicate PrimaryKey values and does not drop them (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:441-443), so dedupe_on_id=false. PrimaryKey has 297,725 distinct values in 297,725 rows (raw_cache_profile.json), so true would give the same result.

Block-group join: the script joins to TIGER 2020 OH block groups with 'within'. It keeps the first match when a point on a boundary matches two block groups, and it drops rows without a 12-digit GEOID (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:461-485). The README reports a 100.00% match and 0 drops (README.md:195-196, 241-242). The runner's tie-break for boundary points may differ.

Output fields the contract cannot carry: the script writes District as 'district' in incidents_bg.parquet (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:499-504). It also cross-checks against the source's CENSUS_BG_GEOID and OffenseDate-derived year as QA only (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:431-433, 487-497). None of these affect which rows are kept.

Coordinates come from the LAT/LON attributes with returnGeometry=false (state/review/packets/city/cleveland/evidence/01_fetch_cleveland.py:357, 446-451). The script never uses feature geometry, so no __arcgis_latitude/__arcgis_longitude fallback is written. If a live pull returns null LAT/LON on a feature that has geometry, the script and the contract both drop that row.

notes: Translation of 01_fetch_cleveland.py. Recomputed on raw_cache.parquet (297,725 rows, 33 columns) with pandas. Stripped-StatDesc map over offense_mapping.csv gives 173,652 mapped rows; all have OffenseYear 2018-2024. The (0,0) filter is included; 13,979 raw rows have null LAT and 0 are at (0,0). Mapped rows with valid LAT/LON number 165,092, and 8,560 are dropped. These counts match README.md:42-49 and the README's 165,092 total (README.md:173). Mapped rows by bucket before the coordinate filter: murder 1,013; rape 3,677; robbery 13,339; aggravated_assault 20,877; burglary 28,007; larceny 79,120; motor_vehicle_theft 27,619. The id is PrimaryKey (CaseNumber plus the offense sequence), so there is one row per offense rather than one per case (README.md:13-17, 264-271). The jurisdiction is Cleveland city (39:municipal:place:3916000). The publisher is the Cleveland Division of Police (README.md:8), and 164,330 of the feed's 2018-2024 incidents fall in Cleveland city per jurisdictions.csv. The other 55 jurisdictions in jurisdictions.csv hold 1-473 incidents each and are spillover, not jurisdictions CPD serves. exclusions_stated_by_publisher is empty. The evidence holds no publisher documentation of exclusions: README.md:250-251 says no layer-level description was available. The block-rounded Address_Public and LAT/LON jitter at README.md:220-236 and 272-277 are the ingester's inferences, not publisher statements. api_endpoint and source_url are the FeatureServer layer URL; the script appends /query ({S}:63-66, 367). The item title reads '2016 to 11/11/25' (README.md:6).
